names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 14 Μαΐου, «Άγιος Ανδρέας ηγούμενος της μονής Ραφαήλ (Τομπόλσκ)», with the rank word left off.

death.note: saint.gr's head line reads «Αγιος Ανδρεας Ηγουμενος Της Μονης Ραφαηλ (τομπολσκ) (; - 1820)»; the body of the page gives no year and no life at all.

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 14ης Μαΐου — «Άγιος Ανδρεας ηγούμενος της μονής Ραφαήλ (Τομπόλσκ)»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 14 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing, and its whole body is one sentence: «Δεν έχουμε λεπτομέρειες για τον βίο του Ρώσου Αγίου» — we have no details of the Russian saint's life. **The only facts are in the calendar line and the head line**: the abbacy, the monastery, the place in brackets and the year 1820, and the `dates` note says the body gives none of it. **He is none of the corpus's Andrews**: nothing in it is an abbot in Siberia. **`abbot` is the only `types` entry** because the office is the only thing said of him; the page does not call him venerable. **The display name keeps the monastery** and not the bracketed Tobolsk, because the monastery is what the line gives him and the bracket is the page's locating gloss; the slug carries Tobolsk, a slug not being a name. It does **not** carry the word abbot, which `types` composes — `draft-saint.mjs` rejected «Andrew, abbot of the Raphael monastery» for exactly that. **No `locations` object.** The page's one link is to the synaxis of all the saints of Siberia, and it cites OCA's feasts and saints.
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue on pravoslavno.rs for the corresponding Julian day (30 September 2026).
